newsitem.title: ITALY: European truckers in protest drive through Milan.
newsitem.headline: European truckers in protest drive through Milan.

text.p: European truckers met on Monday to draw up a platform of demands for their industry, just days after their French colleagues claimed victory in a paralysing strike.
The drivers earlier held a protest drive through the heart of Italy's financial capital Milan.

Fifteen trucks, klaxons blaring and each bearing the flag of a European Union nation, drove slowly through the city to offices where truckers' leaders discussed their main demand for cheaper diesel for the sector.

Delegations from Belgium, Spain and Italy took part in the meeting, organised by the Italian road transport federation FAI. A French delegation had been due to attend but was tied up with negotiations in Paris, a FAI spokeswoman said.
French truck drivers' unions signed a partial accord with employers on Friday after 12 days of national blockades but talks were continuing on the issue of working hours.
"The French strike has only been suspended," FAI secretary-general Paolo Ugge told Reuters, adding negotiations must be concluded by December 15.
"Problems facing Italian truckers are similar to those in other European countries. Our main demand is for tax breaks on fuel. We can't rule out action here," he said.
The Milan meeting will draft a platform of demands for government and European Union action to aid the sector.

"European truckers have the same problems -- high costs and the need for harmonisation of norms and conditions in the sector. Governments and the EU have to realise what the consequences will be if our problems are ignored," Ugge said.
He said as well as the thorny question of lower-taxed fuel which is enjoyed by other sectors like shipping, aviation and agriculture, Italian drivers were facing another problem.
Year-old legislation allowing reimbursement of motorway tolls expires this month and parliament must convert it into law before that date.

"If this doesn't happen, Italian truckers will be forced to take action similar to that seen in France in recent days," Ugge said. "It's possible the Italian road transport industry could come to a halt."
He said European truckers had asked for a meeting with the European parliament in January and were planning further demonstrations "perhaps in every EU member nation's capital."
